services.title: Concrete & Pavers
services.short_description: Driveways, sidewalks, patios, and paver installations built to hold up through NEPA winters.
services.long_description: Concrete work covering driveways, sidewalks, patios, and decorative paver installs, with color, stain, and stamped-pattern options available. Every pour is built to control cracking with a compacted subbase, wire mesh or rebar, controlled water content, and properly spaced control joints, and finished with sealing to protect against salt, acid, and freeze-thaw damage common in Northeastern Pennsylvania.

faqs.q: Can I get a color, stain, or pattern in the concrete?
faqs.a: Yes — flat or textured finishes, stamped patterns, and custom color or stain options are all available. Ask about your own vision for the space.

Concrete does crack, but cracking is controlled with a solid compacted subbase, wire mesh or rebar, a minimum amount of water in the mix, and properly spaced control joints (typically 1/3 the depth of the pour, spaced at roughly three times the concrete's thickness). These joints let the material shrink and flex where intended instead of cracking randomly.

faqs.q: Can you strengthen the concrete so it lasts?
faqs.a: Yes — using a minimum amount of water, adding wire mesh or steel rebar grids, and mixing in fiberglass for extra strength all help. Proper subgrade preparation (compacting the soil or adding tightly packed crushed material) is just as important, and concrete should never be poured on frozen ground or allowed to freeze within 3 days of the pour.

faqs.q: How do you care for concrete?
faqs.a: Concrete is durable and low-maintenance, but acids and salts can deteriorate it over time. Sealing protects against water, dust, UV, and abrasion, and normal dirt, rust, or stains can be cleaned off. Sealing cracks and joints helps minimize water intrusion.

services.title: Retaining Walls
services.short_description: Structural and decorative retaining walls that hold back soil and add usable outdoor living space.
services.long_description: Retaining walls built for both function and appearance — from structural, load-bearing walls to intricate terraced walls to simple planter-box walls for decoration. Every wall is engineered to last while adding interest to the landscape or creating and separating outdoor living spaces.

services.title: Stone, Brick & Stucco
services.short_description: Masonry veneer for full exteriors, accent walls, interior walls, and chimney and basement-wall parging.
services.long_description: Masonry surfaces built for durability, beauty, and water and weather resistance — whether it's an entire home exterior, just the front for curb appeal, an interior accent wall, or a fireplace. Work also includes parging chimneys and basement walls, inside or out, to strengthen and clean up the surface.

services.title: Fireplaces & Chimneys
services.short_description: Custom stone and brick fireplace builds and chimney masonry work.
services.long_description: Custom fireplace and chimney masonry, from full stone fireplace builds to chimney repair and parging work.

team_members.name: Joe Dougher
team_members.bio: Joe started in the masonry trade at 12 years old, helping his stepfather Dave of Dave Jones Masonry, working summers and weekends through school. After graduation he worked with Jim Brunt Masonry and Hudack Masonry Waterproofing, then spent 8 years in the Bricklayers Union Local 5 before starting his own business. 35+ years in the field, licensed (PA088400) and insured.

Cracking is controlled with a solid compacted subbase, wire mesh or rebar, minimal water in the mix, and properly spaced control joints.

faqs.q: Can you strengthen the concrete so it lasts?
faqs.a: Yes — minimal water content, wire mesh or steel rebar, fiberglass reinforcement, and proper subgrade preparation all add strength and longevity.

faqs.a: Concrete is durable and low-maintenance, but sealing protects it from salt, acid, water, and UV damage, and helps prevent staining.

faqs.q: Will the concrete be smooth and perfect when installed?
faqs.a: Concrete is not a manufactured product, so minor imperfections are normal — many clients are drawn to decorative concrete for that character.
